nodes.name: Read Vendor Status
nodes.notes:
Read-only, and the whole reason this workflow exists as more than one SQL statement:
public.campaign_status collapses Bison's `paused` and `archived` into `stopped` / `completed`, and
that is exactly the distinction between "can be revived" and "cannot".

onError: continueRegularOutput — one client's stale key must not end the run for the other twelve.

parameters.query:
insert into public.integration_sync_runs
  (provider, sync_type, n8n_execution_id, status, started_at, finished_at, metadata)
values ('bison', 'ooo_campaign_revive', $1, $2, now(), now(), $3::jsonb)
on conflict (n8n_execution_id) do nothing
returning id;

nodes.name: Resume Campaign
nodes.notes:
THE ONLY WRITE IN THIS WORKFLOW, and it is not a small one: resuming a campaign releases
every contact that piled up inside it while it was paused, at once. Measured 2026-08-20, UniTalk's
`male` campaign held 150 waiting contacts and `female` 76.

That is the intended behaviour — those people replied "I am away until <date>" and the date has
passed — and it is why the audit row records the queue size per campaign. If a burst ever needs
pacing, the lever is the campaign's own max_new_leads_per_day, not this node.

Reached only when the VENDOR says `paused`. Never for `archived`: there is no endpoint that undoes
archiving (probed 2026-08-20 — /unarchive and /restore both 404).

nodes.name: Schedule Trigger
nodes.notes:
Daily, 06:40 UTC — before the Warsaw working day, and off the hourly :15 slot that
bison-campaign-sync occupies. Frequency is deliberately low: a campaign that Bison paused stays
paused, so checking more often buys nothing and only widens the window for fighting a human who is
mid-edit.

nodes.name: Select Routed OOO Campaigns
nodes.notes:
No alwaysOutputData on purpose. With zero candidates it would emit one EMPTY item, and
the next node would build https://go.gheads.com/api/campaigns/undefined and call it. An
empty result must stop the chain, not travel down it.

The cost is that a run with nothing to check writes no audit row. That is acceptable here
and only here: zero candidates means every routed OOO campaign is already active, and the
run itself is still visible in n8n's execution history.

parameters.query:
-- The candidate set: an OOO campaign that an ACTIVE routing rule points at, for a client who
-- actually runs OOO, and whose local copy says it is not sending.
--
-- Local status is only a CHEAP FILTER here, never the verdict. public.campaign_status collapses the
-- two vendor states that decide everything -- Bison's `paused` becomes our `stopped` and its
-- `archived` becomes our `completed` -- and one is revivable while the other has no API to revive it
-- with. The vendor is re-read per campaign in the next node.
--
-- auto_ooo_enabled is required. A client with OOO switched off routes nothing, so reviving their
-- campaigns achieves nothing and would be this workflow overruling an explicit human decision.
-- (Measured 2026-08-20: that guard excludes GIC, whose three campaigns are dead by choice.)
select distinct
       k.id::text               as campaign_id,
       k.external_id            as external_id,
       k.name                   as campaign_name,
       k.status::text           as local_status,
       c.id::text               as client_id,
       c.name                   as client_name,
       cs.api_key               as api_key
  from public.client_ooo_routing r
  join public.campaigns      k  on k.id = r.campaign_id
  join public.clients        c  on c.id = r.client_id
  join public.client_sequencers cs on cs.client_id = c.id and cs.enabled
  join public.sequencers      s on s.id = cs.sequencer_id and s.key = 'emailbison'
 where r.is_active
   and k.archived_at is null
   and k.status <> 'active'
   and c.archived_at is null
   and c.auto_ooo_enabled
   and coalesce(cs.api_key, '') <> ''
 order by c.name, k.name;
